## Design

### 2026-11-08: ### What did you work on?

**12h**

### What did you work on?
This entry covers my cumulative research, learning, and circuit design phase across this entire week. Before I could place any gates in Digital or write Verilog modules, I had to systematically learn how a processor functions from fundamental logic gates up to the full RV32I specification.

I spread this research over several days, breaking down how logic gates form an ALU, how register files manage state without bus conflicts, how instruction bits are split up by a decoder, and how synchronous serial interfaces (like SPI for SD cards) operate at the hardware level.

Here are the main resources and video tutorials I studied throughout the week:
- Ben Eater's 8-bit computer series (logic gates, bus architecture, and stepping logic):
  - ALU & logic gates: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=wvJc9CZcvBc
  - Registers & Bus transfer: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=QzWW-CBugZo
  - Program Counter design: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=g_1HyxBzjl0
- Crash Course Computer Science (high-level CPU concepts & datapath breakdown):
  - How Computers Calculate - The ALU (#5): https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=1I5ZMmrOfnA
  - Registers and RAM (#6): https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=fpnE6UAfbtU
  - The Central Processing Unit / CPU (#7): https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=FZGugFqdr60
- Inside Embedded | Polezero (hardware communication protocols):
  - Serial Communication Explained (UART, I2C & SPI): https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Xik_uetzn2M
- Sebastian Lague's visual logic breakdowns ("How Computers Calculate"):
  - https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=QZwneRb-zqA
- HNeemann's Digital documentation and tutorials for hierarchical sub-circuits and bus splitters.
- The official RISC-V Unprivileged Spec (Volume 1) for exact RV32I opcode bitfields and immediate encoding.

### What worked?
- Building the ALU in steps: first a 1-bit slice, chaining it to 16 bits, and combining two into the full 32-bit ALU with a Zero-flag.
- Setting up the 32 registers so that x0 is hardwired to 0 (which RISC-V strictly requires).
- The instruction decoder and program counter logic both simulated cleanly once wired up.
- Setting up the SPI shift-register timing logic for peripheral communication.

### What didn't work?
- RISC-V branch immediates (B-type) were a headache. The bits aren't stored in order in the instruction word (bits 12, 11, 10:5, 4:1 are scattered all over the place). At first, my sign extension connected them backwards, so branches kept jumping to completely random addresses until I re-checked the spec table.
- Subtraction in the ALU gave me simulation errors at first because two multiplexer select lines were active at the same time, causing wire conflicts. Had to clean up the control logic truth table.
- I had some latch timing issues in the register file where values would loop back and corrupt themselves; switching strictly to edge-triggered D-flip-flops fixed it.

### Schematics & Progress Proof

- **Top-Level RV32I CPU Datapath:** Full integration of Program Counter, instruction ROM, register file, ALU, and instruction decoder.
![cpu](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/e6hGjTGUbsnE3ZfrRWC0EZfD7cDoesW5/6e2d997f0982664ba5a2d4e4e16f21d3f949387c49dd553edf3f6427c43cf8a3.jpg)

- **Sign-Extension Subsystem:** Dedicated circuit handling 32-bit sign extension for I-type, S-type, and scrambled B-type branch immediates.
![sign_extend](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/e6hGjTGUbsnE3ZfrRWC0EZfD7cDoesW5/01652ed64591fbffaf74f2bcd0cdd6c3647c4ae08e1ec922f44ba0e0a41d304c.jpg)

- **32-Register File:** Edge-triggered 32-bit register file featuring dual read ports, a single write port, and a hardware-grounded `x0 = 0` line.
![registers](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/e6hGjTGUbsnE3ZfrRWC0EZfD7cDoesW5/0f30d44d31b700713fdb15432189857bdca83eb9e851fd52535e1596625f1da3.jpg)

- **Program Counter (PC):** Synchronous instruction counter equipped with multiplexers for relative branching, absolute jumps, and reset logic.
![pc](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/e6hGjTGUbsnE3ZfrRWC0EZfD7cDoesW5/8b056c1e8611bc00dd9280c04272001d073cc2a8f3416d74eea32268df5b724a.jpg)

- **Instruction Decoder:** Splits the raw 32-bit instruction word into standard RISC-V fields: opcode, register indices (`rd`, `rs1`, `rs2`), and function codes (`funct3`, `funct7`).
![instruction_decoder](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/e6hGjTGUbsnE3ZfrRWC0EZfD7cDoesW5/0d63c481a696bd4447b3fee5e764292cd6a00ae032e5bbc98d7a849670a35975.jpg)

- **Control Unit:** Decodes instruction opcodes into synchronous datapath control lines for ALU operations, register write-enables, and branch multiplexers.
![control_unit](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/e6hGjTGUbsnE3ZfrRWC0EZfD7cDoesW5/b855c4a3e5c2f665bf04bdec19f08dd5c0436cc391de7f15f2ea7cad72c60d28.jpg)

- **32-Bit ALU Stage:** Core execution block handling addition, two's complement subtraction, bitwise logic gates, and zero-flag detection.
![alu_32bit](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/e6hGjTGUbsnE3ZfrRWC0EZfD7cDoesW5/121876b97ebb6f67b822b97c747afa5cfd189bd05f765968fa1439c03de2b10d.jpg)

- **16-Bit ALU Stage:** Cascaded intermediate block chaining 1-bit slices to verify carry propagation and reduce ripple delay.
![alu_16bit](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/e6hGjTGUbsnE3ZfrRWC0EZfD7cDoesW5/aeeb848f2fe7756143651621fc07228471d5fefc5f4bbbd2b7a59e35fa1912f5.jpg)

- **1-Bit ALU Slice:** Fundamental bit-slice unit featuring a full adder, subtraction borrow logic, and boolean multiplexer selection.
![alu_1bit](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/e6hGjTGUbsnE3ZfrRWC0EZfD7cDoesW5/e5547da2da70229acf7805a2eea4eb66a4354514564f709fc7f265534f282e57.jpg)

- **nextpnr-gowin Terminal Output:** Successful place-and-route run meeting a 44.34 MHz timing closure (0 errors, 3 warnings) targeting the Tang Nano 9K.
![Nextpnr_terminal_output](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/e6hGjTGUbsnE3ZfrRWC0EZfD7cDoesW5/7d929764d3804ef8a831c94d78af25f40ba0121bf764bfb85007319827e3fa80.jpg)
